analysis.evidence: The feminine singular verb agrees with הָאָרֶץ, “the earth.” The parallel clause says that the earth was filled with חָמָס, “violence,” identifying the corruption in view.
analysis.morphology: Niphal wayyiqtol, third person feminine singular, with prefixed וַ־

analysis.evidence: הָאָרֶץ is the subject of וַתִּשָּׁחֵת, “became corrupt.” The parallel clause says the earth was filled with violence, showing that the first occurrence refers to the inhabited world.
analysis.morphology: Common noun, singular absolute, with the definite article הָ־ and feminine singular agreement.

analysis.evidence: In וַתִּשָּׁחֵת הָאָרֶץ לִפְנֵי הָאֱלֹהִים, לִפְנֵי takes הָאֱלֹהִים as its complement. The earth had become corrupt in God’s sight.
analysis.morphology: Compound preposition formed from prefixed לְ (here לִ־) and פְנֵי, the common plural construct of פָּנִים.
analysis.sense: before, in the presence of (a person, Yahweh)

analysis.evidence: לִפְנֵי הָאֱלֹהִים means “before God.” The earth had become corrupt in God’s sight, and the following clause describes that corruption by saying the earth was filled with violence.
analysis.morphology: Definite article הָ־ prefixed to a masculine plural noun in the absolute state, with singular reference.

analysis.evidence: וַתִּמָּלֵא agrees with its feminine singular subject הָאָרֶץ, “the earth.” חָמָס names what filled it: “and the earth was filled with violence.”
analysis.morphology: Niphal wayyiqtol, third-person feminine singular, with prefixed וַ and no suffix

analysis.evidence: In וַתִּמָּלֵא הָאָרֶץ חָמָס, “the earth was filled with violence,” the marked noun is the subject of the feminine singular verb וַתִּמָּלֵא. It refers to the same earth described as corrupt in the first clause.
analysis.morphology: Definite article הָ־ prefixed to a singular absolute noun, construed as feminine here.

analysis.evidence: In וַתִּמָּלֵא הָאָרֶץ חָמָס, “the earth was filled with violence,” הָאָרֶץ is the subject and חָמָס names what filled it. The preceding clause describes the earth as corrupt before God, and the image of filling portrays the violence as pervasive.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular absolute noun, without prefix or suffix.
